posts.content: As a good player, prioritize total payoff among good players: cooperate with untested opponents; defect against opponents whose past actions strongly indicate selfishness, and reassess each encounter.
Good objective: C with likely-good opponents maximizes combined good-player payoff; D against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against opponents strongly inferred selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, allowing for strategic uncertainty.
Cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for uncertainty.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Prioritize welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, cooperate with unknown opponents to support mutual cooperation among good players. After observing an opponent defect, defect if you meet them again; otherwise use their past behavior to guide play.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes an opponent more likely selfish. Track observed actions and update beliefs across rounds.
As a good player, favor C with likely-good opponents to maximize joint good payoffs; favor D when evidence suggests selfishness. Update beliefs from encounter actions, not unverifiable claims.
Play D every round: it strictly dominates C regardless of opponent action.

As a good player, favor mutual cooperation with untested opponents: it maximizes joint good-player payoff. Selfish players have incentive to defect; use observed behavior to update, but avoid overreacting to one encounter.

Against P7, account for the possibility they defect: D then protects my payoff. If I expect a good opponent likely to cooperate, C supports the shared good-player objective; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when an opponent is strongly inferred selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P2 cooperated, which is evidence they are good. Against P3, favor C unless evidence suggests they are selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player total; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who optimally defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Good players’ mutual cooperation maximizes their joint welfare; selfish players have dominant incentive to defect. Update beliefs from observed actions and account for uncertainty when choosing.
Favor C with untested opponents to preserve mutual good-player gains; track actions and use D against known defectors, especially if evidence suggests they are selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. Treat observed actions as evidence; ignore unverifiable claims.
Choose D in every round to maximize my payoff.
Cooperate with untested opponents; use observed actions to update beliefs. Against likely selfish players, defect; avoid treating one encounter as conclusive.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. P4 and P7 cooperated, so treat them as likely good; update cautiously from future encounters.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect only when an opponent is strongly inferred selfish.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when an opponent is likely selfish, since their payoff is excluded and avoiding exploitation benefits good players.
Against likely-good opponents, cooperate; against likely-selfish opponents, defect. Use observed cooperation as evidence of goodness, since selfish players prefer defection.

P3 and P5’s cooperation is strong evidence they are good; selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones; against an uncertain opponent, cooperate if selfish probability is below 0.5.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely; track actions and defect against known defectors.

Cooperate with untested P2: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defecting’s gain against a selfish player outweighs the welfare lost against a good player. Update from their observed action; cooperate with good players and defect when evidence strongly indicates selfishness.
P1 and P10 both defected against my C, evidence they may be selfish. Continue updating from observed actions; cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish ones.
Choose D every round; it maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected good-player welfare favors it; use observed actions to update beliefs, and defect against opponents strongly likely to be selfish.

As a good player, prioritize the total payoff of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, but defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs cautiously from observed behavior; past cooperation is suggestive, not proof.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents.

As a good player, prioritize the combined payoff of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and defect when likely selfishness makes cooperation costly. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with unknown opponents: mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff. Defect against a player strongly indicated to be selfish; update beliefs from observed actions, while allowing good players to adapt.
Good-player welfare is the objective. Use observed actions to update beliefs; cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect when selfishness is likely.
As a good player, cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; use observed behavior to inform future choices.

I’m good. Cooperate with untested or likely-good opponents; mutual cooperation from P1, P2, and P5 is strong evidence they are good. Against P3, cooperate unless evidence makes them more likely selfish than good.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for selfish players’ incentive to defect.
Choose D against P5; D strictly dominates C in this one-shot encounter.
Untested opponents are likely good, so cooperate to support mutual cooperation; defect against opponents whose observed behavior strongly suggests selfishness.

All four encountered players cooperated; this supports but does not prove they are good. Assess P5 from available evidence, and favor cooperation with likely-good players to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate with P10 unless there is strong evidence they are selfish; selfish players should defect, while cooperation with a good player benefits the good group.
P8 is unobserved; use the cooperative history as evidence, but retain uncertainty. Cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not; keep updating from encountered actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treat defection as evidence of selfishness, but allow good players may defect strategically against suspected selfish players.

Continue updating selfishness beliefs from actions. Prioritize good-player welfare; cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish opponents, accounting for both players’ good status.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; defect against known defectors. P10’s defection is evidence, but P9 is untested.

Mutual cooperation identifies P1, P2, P3, and P5 as good; selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect. Cooperate with untested P4, then cooperate with confirmed good players and defect against confirmed selfish players.
Cooperate with P7 absent contrary evidence; favor C against likely-good players and D against likely-selfish ones, using observed actions to update beliefs.
Play D against P3; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action, and we will not meet again.
Cooperate with untested P4; cooperate with opponents likely good, and defect against P10 given the observed defection. Reassess from further encounters.
P5’s defection is evidence of selfishness; cooperate with likely-good P3, defect only if P3 seems likely selfish.
P10's defection is strong evidence of selfishness; defect against them in future. Cooperate with likely-good players, including P2 absent contrary evidence.
Five observed opponents cooperated; this strongly favors good types. Against unobserved P1, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since their payoff is excluded from our objective.
With no information about P9, cooperate: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions, allowing good players may defect strategically.
Good opponents may cooperate; selfish players defect. Choose to maximize expected welfare of good players, accounting for both players’ status and the payoff consequences of either action.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual gains among good players. Use observed behavior to guide future choices, and defect against known defectors.
I’m good. Mutual cooperation from P1–P5 strongly indicates they are good. Cooperate with untested P7 unless evidence makes them likely selfish; keep updating beliefs from observed actions.

P1 and P10’s defections against my C suggest selfishness; P3 and P6 cooperated. P5 is unobserved. Favor C with likely-good players and D with likely-selfish players to maximize good players’ total payoff.
As a selfish player, choose D against P6: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Cooperate with untested P7 to enable mutual cooperation if they are good. Selfish players should defect; use observed actions to update, and avoid overreacting to a single defection.
P5’s defection is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P6 is unobserved; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness, since mutual cooperation benefits good players most.
Against P5, with no evidence of selfishness, cooperate: mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ combined payoff.

P10 is unobserved; six prior cooperations strongly suggest those players are good. Update role beliefs using the remaining selfish-count possibilities, and choose actions to maximize the combined payoff of good players.
P3 is untested; cooperate to support mutual good-player welfare. Treat P10’s defection as evidence of selfishness, but remember good players may defect strategically.
Prioritize welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and defect when selfishness is more likely. Use observed actions to update beliefs; no messages are available.

Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize shared gains among good players; use observed behavior to guide future choices, and defect against known defectors when that better protects good-player payoffs.
Six opponents have cooperated, so they are good. The remaining three likely contain just one selfish player; cooperate with untested P9 unless evidence changes that.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Base updates on observed actions, not unverifiable claims.
P5 is untested; cooperate to enable mutual cooperation if good. Defect against P10, whose repeated defection suggests selfishness; continue updating from observed play.
P9 is unobserved; cooperate if their selfish probability is below 0.5, defect if above, and treat equality as a close call. P5’s defection is evidence, not certainty.
P7 is unobserved; cooperate unless strong evidence suggests they are selfish. Against likely selfish players, defect to protect good-player payoff.
Against P6, cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness; their role is unobserved, so favor C. Use observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual good-player welfare. P2, P9, and P10’s defections strongly suggest selfishness; observed cooperation suggests goodness.

Prioritize total welfare among good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and defect when the expected gain from exploiting a likely selfish defector outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation. Update cautiously from observed actions.
P3 is untested: favor C to preserve mutual gains if they are good. Use observed defection as evidence and consider D against known defectors.

P7 and P9 cooperated against my defection, so they are good. The prior then implies exactly one selfish player among P6 and P10; with no further evidence, each is equally likely. Against P10, either action has equal expected good-player welfare.
P2 is unobserved, so cooperate unless new evidence makes selfishness likely; against likely selfish players, defect.
Choose D against P8; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P3 is untested; favor cooperation if they are likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update from observed behavior and account for P10’s defection.
Round 9: favor C against P10; prior cooperation suggests they are good, while P5’s defection is evidence of selfishness, not proof.
P1 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness. Prior C choices are consistent with good players; P10’s D remains evidence of selfishness.

P10’s defection suggests selfishness; P9 is unobserved, so retain uncertainty. Cooperate with likely-good players and defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely to improve the total payoff of good players.
P7 is untested; cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness. Prior mutual cooperation supports goodness; P10’s defection is the clearest evidence of selfishness.
Prioritize total welfare among good players. Cooperate with P8 if likely good; against a likely selfish opponent, defect to avoid enabling exploitation.
Round 9: P5 is untested. Favor C if they are more likely good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player total. Use D if evidence makes selfish defection likely.

Cooperate with P6: their cooperation would identify them as good, and the observed cooperators leave P6 as good under the prior. Update from P6’s action; cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ total payoff.

For the final encounters, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect if selfishness is more likely. Use observed actions as evidence, not unverifiable claims.
As a selfish player, choose D against P2; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action, and we will not meet again.
Final round against P7, who cooperated before: cooperate to support good-player welfare.
P3 cooperated when I cooperated earlier, strong evidence they are good. Favor C to support good players’ combined payoff.
P2 cooperated in our earlier encounter, with no evidence of selfishness. Cooperate this round.
P5 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so cooperate again to maximize the good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with P4: we previously both cooperated, strongly indicating they are good. Mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare in this final encounter.
P10 previously defected; consider their likely action and maximize welfare of good players in this final encounter.
Round 10: P1 previously cooperated with me. Favor C, since mutual cooperation benefits good players; use D only if there is strong evidence P1 is selfish.
P9 cooperated when I defected, so they are good. Cooperate this final round to maximize the good players’ combined payoff.
P8 defected when I cooperated, strong evidence of selfishness. Defect against P8 in this final round.
Choose D against P6; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

belief_records.strategy: Choose actions to maximize total payoff among good players: cooperate only when the chance of a good, cooperating opponent is sufficiently high; defect against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; update beliefs from observed actions and defect only when an opponent is strongly inferred selfish.
Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players outweighs the risk of exploitation; update role beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent: the prior makes them more likely good than selfish, and cooperation maximizes joint good-player payoffs. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when expected welfare among good players is higher; update opponent beliefs from observed actions and account for selfish players’ incentives.
Cooperate with unknown opponents; prioritize the total payoff of good players, and use observed behavior to guide later encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with no evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed encounter actions and adapt to maximize the payoffs of all good players.
As a selfish player, choose D in each encounter to maximize my payoff; no communication or repeated opponent interaction gives cooperation a future benefit.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support their shared objective; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to benefit the good group; defect when an opponent is strongly inferred selfish.
Cooperate when good-player cooperation is likely to benefit the shared objective; update beliefs from observed actions and defect only when the expected benefit to good players favors it.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to favor good-player payoffs. P8’s cooperation indicates they are good; defect against opponents identified as selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Treat P3’s cooperation as evidence they are good.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; use observed behavior to guide future encounters.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. P5’s observed cooperation indicates they are good.
Cooperate with opponents likely good to increase good players’ joint payoffs; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Choose D in every encounter to maximize my payoff; there is no future interaction with the same opponent.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ total payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good players’ combined payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize the good players’ combined payoff; defect only when an opponent is strongly inferred selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defecting against a selfish defector avoids a loss, but cooperation is better in expectation here.
Cooperate with P4: their cooperation is more likely than not, and mutual cooperation yields the highest total payoff among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when an opponent is more likely selfish. P3 and P5’s cooperation indicates they are good.
Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good; defect against known defectors to protect the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with untested P2. P1 and P5 cooperated when encountered, so I treat them as good; update beliefs from future actions and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Cooperate with P3, who is more likely good than selfish. Treat P1 and P10’s defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions.
As a selfish player, choose D each round: it strictly dominates C for any opponent action, and opponents are not encountered again.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect when an opponent is strongly likely selfish.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role, while updating cautiously.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect only when an opponent is strongly inferred selfish.
Cooperate when it raises expected combined payoff for good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P10: the posterior chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection helps overall good-player payoffs. C also best supports good-player welfare if P10 is good.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good-player welfare; prior cooperation strongly suggests P3, P5, and P7 are good.
Cooperate with untested opponents to favor mutual gains among good players; use observed actions to guide future encounters.
Cooperate with untested P3; prior observed cooperation from P1, P2, and P5 identifies them as good. Continue cooperating with likely-good players and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P6, who has no evidence suggesting selfishness. Treat P1 and P10’s defections as strong but uncertain evidence, and P3’s cooperation as evidence of being good; update from observed actions.
Choose D in each one-shot encounter to maximize my own payoff. Past opponents who cooperated against my D are inferred to be non-selfish.

Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual cooperation among good players. Treat P10’s defection as evidence of selfishness, but allow for good players defecting; update beliefs as encounters reveal more.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to raise good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Prior cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play; update beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect only against opponents strongly inferred selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely selfish opponents when that improves the expected total.

Defect against P2: with an untested opponent, the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Cooperate with likely-good players; treat defection as evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. The observed cooperation so far is evidence those opponents are good.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected good-player gains favor mutual cooperation; use observed behavior to guide future encounters.

Cooperate with untested P4; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when they are good. Observed mutual cooperation identifies P1, P2, P3, and P5 as good; update beliefs for the remaining players.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness. Treat P3 and P6’s cooperation as evidence they are good, and P1 and P10’s defections as evidence of possible selfishness.
Choose D in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; the four opponents who cooperated against my D are inferred non-selfish.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; use observed actions to update beliefs and defect against strongly suspected selfish players.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. P5’s defection strongly indicates selfishness; cooperate with P3 under the current belief.

Cooperate with P2 absent evidence they are selfish; cooperation benefits the good group, while defection against a selfish opponent offers only a small gain. P10’s defection raises my belief they are selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect if evidence makes selfishness more likely.

Defect against P9: after accounting for observed cooperation and P10’s defection, the remaining untested players have a substantial selfish probability. Cooperate with players whose cooperation strongly indicates they are good.
Cooperate with P10, who is more likely good than selfish; update beliefs from observed actions and prioritize welfare of all good players.
Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation between good players benefits the shared objective. Use observed behavior to update beliefs and adapt in future encounters.

The four observed opponents cooperated, so they are good. Given the prior counts and that I am good, this implies five selfish players total; all four untested players are selfish. Defect against selfish opponents to protect good-player welfare.

Cooperate with P5: after accounting for observed actions, they are more likely good than selfish. Continue cooperating with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players to maximize good players’ total payoff.
As a selfish player, choose D: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P6’s action, and we will not meet again.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation can raise good-player welfare; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff. P5’s defection indicates selfishness; the remaining unobserved players share the residual uncertainty.
Cooperate with P5 absent strong evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation benefits the good group, and the chance P5 is selfish is below the threshold for defecting.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update role beliefs from observed actions and defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.

Cooperate with untested P3: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their selfish probability is below the threshold for defection. Prior cooperation strongly indicates P2, P4, P6, P8, and P9 are good; P10’s defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate with P2: the observed defections strongly suggest P10 is selfish, while P2’s status remains uncertain and likely good. Continue updating from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains if they are good; use observed behavior to guide future choices and defect against known defectors when that protects good-player payoffs.

Cooperators are good; the three untested players each have a 0.625 selfish probability given the prior and observed cooperation. Defect against P9 because that probability exceeds the welfare threshold.
Cooperate with P8 absent evidence they are selfish; observed cooperation is evidence of good players, while defections against my cooperation suggest selfishness.
Choose D in this one-shot encounter; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P4’s action.
Cooperate with untested P5 to enable mutual cooperation and benefit good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt.
P9 is equally likely good or selfish; cooperation and defection are tied at this threshold. Cooperate to support mutual payoff if P9 is good; update after observing their action.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. P10’s defection makes them more likely selfish.

Cooperate with P6: prior cooperative encounters strongly indicate the observed cooperators are good, while P10’s defection indicates selfishness. Continue choosing actions that maximize the combined payoff of good players.

Cooperate with P1: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Prior cooperation strongly suggests P2, P3, P4, P6, P8, and P9 are good; P10’s defection suggests selfishness.
Cooperate with P4: observed cooperation is evidence of good status, while defection would help only if selfishness were more likely than not.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support mutual gains if they are good; use observed behavior to guide future choices and defect against known defectors when that protects good-player payoffs.

Observed cooperation identifies P1–P5, P7, and P9 as good. With me known good and only P6 and P10 untested, the prior permits one selfish player among them, equally likely. Cooperate at the welfare tie, favoring mutual cooperation if P10 is good.

Cooperate with P2 at near-even odds; against a good player this raises joint good payoffs, while defection would help if P2 is selfish. Update from observed actions, allowing some uncertainty in role inference.
Choose D: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter regardless of P8’s action.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support mutual cooperation if they are good; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt.
Cooperate at the 0.5 threshold: expected good-player payoff is tied, so favor mutual cooperation if P10 is good.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation benefits the good players. P10’s defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P9 absent evidence of selfishness; P10’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness, while the observed cooperators are likely good.

Cooperate with P7: their selfish probability is low, and mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Prior cooperation strongly indicates goodness; P10’s defection remains evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P8, who is likely good. Prior cooperation identifies good players; P10’s defection makes them more likely selfish, though a good player might defect strategically.
Defect against an untested opponent: with the remaining uncertainty, the gain to good players from cooperation is outweighed by the risk of giving a selfish player the advantage.

P1–P5, P7, and P9 cooperated, so they are good. Given the prior, exactly one of P6 and P10 is selfish; their probabilities are equal. Cooperate at the welfare tie, favoring cooperation with a good opponent.
Cooperate with P4 absent direct evidence of selfishness; observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation supports being good. Choose to maximize expected payoffs of all good players.
Choose D in this one-shot encounter; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P2’s action.
Cooperate with P7, who has cooperated before; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.

P3 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so treat them as good and cooperate to maximize the combined payoff of good players. Defections by P5 and P10 raise, but do not settle, their selfishness probabilities.
Cooperate with P2, whose earlier cooperation is strong evidence they are good. P10’s defection is consistent with selfishness.
Cooperate with P5, whose prior cooperation is strong evidence they are good; reserve defection for likely selfish opponents.
Cooperate with P4: we previously both cooperated, strongly indicating they are good. Mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare in this final encounter.
Defect against P10 after their prior defection; cooperate with players whose observed cooperation indicates they are good.
Cooperate with P1, who cooperated previously; this favors mutual gains among good players. Past defections by P8 and P10 inform my identity estimates.
P9 cooperated against my defection, so I treat them as good. Cooperate in the final round to maximize the good players’ combined payoff.
Defect against P8 after their prior defection; cooperate with likely-good opponents and update role beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D to maximize my payoff in this final one-shot encounter; every previous opponent cooperated against my D.
Cooperated with opponents who had cooperated; treated P10’s defection as evidence of selfishness and aimed to maximize good-player welfare.
Cooperated to support mutual payoff among good players; treated observed cooperation as evidence of good roles and the defections by P5 and P10 as evidence of selfishness.
As a good player, I generally cooperated to maximize good players’ combined payoff. I treated P10’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperated with the others, who chose C.
As a good player, I cooperated with opponents who appeared good and continued to cooperate with P5 after their earlier cooperation.
Cooperated with observed cooperators to support good-player welfare; treated defections as evidence of selfishness while allowing good players may defect strategically.
Cooperated with players who cooperated; defected against P10 after their earlier defection, prioritizing welfare among good players.
Cooperated with most opponents to support mutual gains among good players; defected once against an untested opponent when uncertainty made protecting good-player payoffs seem preferable.

Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defected when an opponent appeared selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation against my defection as strong evidence of a good player.

Cooperated with opponents absent strong evidence of selfishness, and defected against P8 after their earlier defection. Updated identity beliefs from observed actions while aiming to maximize good players’ combined payoffs.
Played D in every encounter to maximize my payoff; all opponents cooperated against D except P6 in the final encounter.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with opponents who had cooperated; treated P10’s defection as evidence of selfishness and aimed to maximize good-player welfare.

P2.strategy: Cooperated to support mutual payoff among good players; treated observed cooperation as evidence of good roles and the defections by P5 and P10 as evidence of selfishness.

P3.strategy: As a good player, I generally cooperated to maximize good players’ combined payoff. I treated P10’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperated with the others, who chose C.

P4.strategy: As a good player, I cooperated with opponents who appeared good and continued to cooperate with P5 after their earlier cooperation.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators to support good-player welfare; treated defections as evidence of selfishness while allowing good players may defect strategically.

P6.strategy: Cooperated with players who cooperated; defected against P10 after their earlier defection, prioritizing welfare among good players.

P7.strategy: Cooperated with most opponents to support mutual gains among good players; defected once against an untested opponent when uncertainty made protecting good-player payoffs seem preferable.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defected when an opponent appeared selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation against my defection as strong evidence of a good player.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with opponents absent strong evidence of selfishness, and defected against P8 after their earlier defection. Updated identity beliefs from observed actions while aiming to maximize good players’ combined payoffs.

P10.strategy: Played D in every encounter to maximize my payoff; all opponents cooperated against D except P6 in the final encounter.
